title: And Art Thou with Us, Gracious Lord
description: And Art Thou with Us, Gracious Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 627 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Trust in the Presence and Help of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: And art thou with us, gra-cious Lord, To dis-si-pate our fear? Dost thou pro-claim thy-self our God, Our God for-ev-er near?

lines: And art thou with us, gracious Lord,
Dost thou proclaim thyself our God,
Doth thy right hand, which formed the earth,
And bears up all the skies,
Stretch from on high its friendly aid,
On this support our souls shall lean,
The gloomy vale of death will smile,
If God be with us there.
While we his gracious succor prove,
The darkest shades, through which we pass,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
